best_for: Members of open-source projects, research groups and companies already on Zulip who want its topic threads in a desktop app with proper notifications.
description:
Zulip is a team chat app from Kandra Labs, and this desktop app is its official client. It is open source under the Apache-2.0 license, and it is used by groups such as the Rust language community and the Recurse Center.

What sets Zulip apart is that every conversation starts with a short topic, a bit like an email subject. Your inbox then lists the conversations with unread messages, so you can catch up on one thread at a time and reply in context, even days later, instead of scrolling one long channel. Zulip says it makes switching from Slack or Microsoft Teams easy. An organization can also start on Zulip Cloud and move to its own server later.

points.title: A client, not the service
points.text: The app connects to a Zulip organization you already belong to, hosted by Zulip Cloud or on someone's own server. Without one there is nothing to sign in to.

points.title: Several organizations at once
points.text: You can sign in to multiple organizations in one window, reply from desktop notifications, and use a spell checker in several languages. Updates install on their own.

points.title: The app is free; hosting may not be
points.text: Zulip Cloud Free keeps 10,000 messages of search history and 5 GB of files. Standard is USD 6.67 per user per month billed yearly. Open-source projects can get Standard free. Prices were read on the date below.

points.title: Self-hosting stays free
points.text: The server is open source and the free self-hosted plan has every feature. Mobile push notifications are limited to 10 users there unless your community qualifies or you pay for Basic.

points.title: Windows installer choices
points.text: Windows gets an MSI and an .exe installer that can go per-user or machine-wide, all x64. The Windows listing keeps 25 versions.

points.title: macOS and Linux
points.text: macOS has Intel and Apple silicon builds for macOS 13 and later. Linux uses a Flathub build verified for Kandra Labs, for x64 and Arm64. Both list only the current release here.
